### Population counts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Population counts")]

The population count is a stipulation of the Special Recreation Permit (SRP) granted to the Burning Man Project, formerly Black Rock City, LLC (BRC), by the BLM, for the event each year. Originally used to calculate fees, it's now used to ensure that the event does not exceed the maximum authorized population as specified in the SRP. Not everyone at the event is included in the population count. Exempted from the count are government personnel and government contractors; however, this has changed over time.

The population count was originally used to calculate fees owed to the BLM. It was not long until the BLM began considering putting a limit on the number of people that would be allowed to attend the event. This became a point of contention as early as 1998 when the BLM proposed a complicated usage formula, effectively limiting the size of the event to that of the previous year.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Larry-196)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-197)

Starting in 2006, the SRP stipulated that BRC manage "ticket sales in a manner to keep the maximum population of the event from increasing more than 6% above the highest population recorded in a previous year."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):1 Fees were based on the daily population counts of Black Rock City at noon.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):12 This was the first year where fees were explicitly exempted for BRC staff.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):12.

In 2011, the fee structure changed to be based on adjusted gross income and was no longer tied to daily population counts.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-198):5

The 2012 SRP further defined who was to be counted in population counts. The term "participant" was introduced, as defined in that year's Environmental Assessment (EA), to include "all attendees of the event, including paid participants and volunteers. The population does not include government personnel, Humboldt General Hospital emergency service providers, vendors and contractors."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-199):2–1 The maximum authorized population now applied to "participants".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2012-129):1

In 2014, volunteers were explicitly exempted from the population count and the population cap was further refined to now apply to "paid participants".[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2014-139):1

In 2019, the definition of "population" changed again, this time to include BRC staff and volunteers, now collectively referred to as "attendees".[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2019-165):1 This coincided with the necessity of a new Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the 2019–2028 SRP application which introduced this change in definition.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-200):ES-1 The Burning Man Project reported a population of 78,850 for that year, an increase of about 8,600 people from the previous year, noting that "everyone" was now being counted in the maximum population count.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Timeline-201) This roughly correlates with the Burning Man Project's 2019 Form 990 disclosure which states it employs 986 people and has 10,000 volunteers.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-202):1

In 2022, an additional restriction on the total number of attendees for the entirety of the event was introduced. "The cumulative maximum authorized population for the 2022 event is 87,000 total attendees." The maximum number of attendees on the playa at any one time remained as it was in 2019 at 80,000.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2022-179):1

## Principles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Principles")]

![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f2/Edit-clear.svg/40px-Edit-clear.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)This section **contains [too many or overly lengthy quotations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Quotations "Wikipedia:Manual of Style")**. [![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Burning_Man_2011_Victor_Grigas_Man_Burn_IMG_4774.JPG/250px-Burning_Man_2011_Victor_Grigas_Man_Burn_IMG_4774.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burning_Man_2011_Victor_Grigas_Man_Burn_IMG_4774.JPG)

The man effigy with fireworks before being burned in 2011

Because of the variety of goals fostered by participatory attendees, known as "Burners," Burning Man does not have a single focus. Features of the event are subject to the participants and include _community_, _artwork_, _absurdity_, _decommodification_ and _revelry_. Participation is encouraged.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-203)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-204)

The Burning Man event and its affiliated communities are guided by 10 principles meant to evoke the cultural ethos that has emerged from the event. They were originally written by Larry Harvey in 2004[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-205) as guidelines for regional organizing, then later became universal criteria of the general culture of the multifaceted movement. The 10 Principles are:[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-principles-206)

*   radical [inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion_(value_and_practice) "Inclusion (value and practice)")
*   gifting
*   [decommodification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decommodification "Decommodification")
*   radical [self-reliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-sufficiency "Self-sufficiency")
*   radical [self-expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_expression "Emotional expression")
*   [communal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community "Community") effort
*   civic [responsibility](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/responsibility "wikt:responsibility")
*   [leaving no trace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leave_No_Trace "Leave No Trace")
*   participation
*   immediacy

The descriptions in quotes are the actual text:

### Radical inclusion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Radical inclusion")]

"Anyone may be a part of Burning Man. We welcome and respect the stranger. No prerequisites exist for participation in our community." This was written with a broad stroke for general organizing, meaning anyone is welcome to the Burning Man culture. Prerequisites for the Burning Man[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-principles-206) event are: participants are expected to provide for their own basic needs, follow the guidelines in the annually updated event "survival guide", and purchase a $475 ticket to get in.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-survivalguide-207)

### Gifting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Gifting")]

"Burning Man is devoted to acts of gift-giving. The value of a gift is unconditional. Gifting does not contemplate a return or an exchange for something of equal value." Instead of cash, burners are encouraged to rely on a [gift economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gift_economy "Gift economy"), a sort of [potlatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potlatch "Potlatch"). In the earliest days of the event, an underground [barter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barter "Barter") economy also existed, in which burners exchanged "favors" with each other. While this was originally supported by the Burning Man organization, it is now largely discouraged. Instead, burners are encouraged to give one another gifts unconditionally. Despite the efforts of the Burning Man organization, bartering still continues to be very common across certain camps.

### Decommodification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Decommodification")]

"To preserve the spirit of gifting, our community seeks to create social environments that are unmediated by commercial sponsorships, transactions, or advertising. We stand ready to protect our culture from such exploitation. We resist the substitution of consumption for participatory experience." No cash transactions are permitted between burners. Cash can be used for a select few charity, fuel, and sanitation vendors as follows:[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-208)

*   Café beverages such as coffee, [chai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_chai "Masala chai"), [lemonade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemonade "Lemonade"), etc., which are sold at Center Camp Café, operated by the organizers of the event.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-209) Citing cost, decreased need, environmental impact, and decommodification, beverage sales were halted in 2022.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-210)
*   [Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice "Ice") sales benefit the local [Gerlach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerlach,_Nevada "Gerlach, Nevada")-[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire,_Nevada "Empire, Nevada") school system.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-211)
*   Tickets for the shuttle bus to the nearest Nevada communities of Gerlach and Empire which is operated by a contractor not participating in the event: [Green Tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Tortoise "Green Tortoise").[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-212)
*   A reentry wristband, which allows a person to leave and reenter the event and may be purchased at the gate upon exit.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-213)
*   An airport use fee, payable at the airport upon first entry.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-214)
*   Diesel and biodiesel sold by third-party contractors.
*   RV dump service and camp [graywater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graywater "Graywater") disposal service.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-215)
*   Private portable toilets and servicing, which can be arranged with the official contractor.

### Radical self-reliance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Radical self-reliance")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Burning_Man_2012_%287942014474%29.jpg/250px-Burning_Man_2012_%287942014474%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burning_Man_2012_(7942014474).jpg)

Dust storms are common at Burning Man, so many come prepared with appropriate protection such as goggles and masks to reduce dust inhalation.

"Burning Man encourages the individual to discover, exercise, and rely on his or her inner resources." The event's harsh environment and remote location require participants to be responsible for their subsistence. Since the LLC forbids most commerce, participants must be prepared and bring all their own supplies with the exception of the items stated in Decommodification.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-216) Public portable toilets are also available throughout the city; some of these are, like art cars, decorated in imaginative ways by volunteers.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-217)

### Radical self-expression

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Radical self-expression")]

[Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b7/Trojan_Horse_Pull_-_Burning_Man_2011.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Trojan Horse Pull – Burning Man 2011

"Radical self-expression arises from the unique gifts of the individual. No one other than the individual or a collaborating group can determine its content. It is offered as a gift to others. In this spirit, the giver should respect the rights and liberties of the recipient." Burners are encouraged to express themselves in a number of ways through various art forms and projects. The event is clothing-optional and [public nudity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_nudity "Public nudity") is common, though not practiced by the majority.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-OpenSex-218)[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Illicit_Activities-219)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-220)

### Communal effort

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Communal effort")]

"Our community values creative cooperation and collaboration. We strive to produce, promote and protect social networks, public spaces, works of art, and methods of communication that support such interaction." Burners are encouraged to work with and help one another.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-participate-221)

### Civic responsibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Civic responsibility")]

"We value civil society. Community members who organize events should assume responsibility for public welfare and endeavor to communicate civic responsibilities to participants. They must also assume responsibility for conducting events in accordance with local, state and federal laws."

### Leave no trace

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Leave no trace")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg/250px-Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg)

Burning Man Playa Restoration 2015 – attendees carry sticks and buckets to clean the desert of MOOP (matter out of place), as part of the "leave no trace" policy.

"Our community respects the environment. We are committed to leaving no physical trace of our activities wherever we gather. We clean up after ourselves and endeavor, whenever possible, to leave such places in a better state than when we found them."

### Participation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Participation")]

"Our community is committed to a radically participatory ethic. We believe that transformative change, whether in the individual or in society, can occur only through the medium of deeply personal participation. We achieve being through doing. Everyone is invited to work. Everyone is invited to play. We make the world real through actions that open the heart." People are encouraged to participate, rather than observe.

### Immediacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Immediacy")]

"Immediate experience is, in many ways, the most important touchstone of value in our culture. We seek to overcome barriers that stand between us and a recognition of our inner selves, the reality of those around us, participation in society, and contact with a natural world exceeding human powers. No idea can substitute for this experience."

## The Temple

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: The Temple")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Temple_Burn_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-Temple_Burn_-_panoramio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Temple_Burn_-_panoramio.jpg)

Temple of Stars, burning, 2004

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Burning_Man_Temple_2021.jpg/250px-Burning_Man_Temple_2021.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burning_Man_Temple_2021.jpg)

Temple of Constraints, 2021

The Temple is the secondary major recurring art installation at Burning Man after the Man, and is considered just as important to the event culture. According to the Burning Man Project, "The Temple is a community shared space that is an important part of Black Rock City. It is not a temple in recognition of any religion; it's a neutral, non-denominational spiritual space where everyone can gather to share in the experience of remembering the past, honoring or cursing the present, and pondering the future to come."[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Black_Rock_City_Temple_Grant-222)

The prime function of the Temple is to be a canvas upon which people can leave words and objects behind to be burned, and to serve as "a place of contemplation, a place to rest, a place of reflection, a place of rituals, weddings, reunions, etc".[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-223) During the event, 400 volunteer Temple Guardians monitor the Temple 24 hours a day.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-224) The Temple is burned on the eighth and final night of the event, following the "Man burn" on the previous night.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Black_Rock_City_Temple_Grant-222)

### Temple Builders Guild

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Temple Builders Guild")]

The Temple Builders Guild (TBG) is a U.S.-based nonprofit public arts organization founded in 2020 by Thomas J. Lee and Nick Morgan—both experienced temple build crew members—to support the construction of large-scale community and municipal art projects, particularly the Temple at Burning Man. Established in response to the recurring logistical challenges faced by annual Temple builders, the organization was created to provide shared infrastructure, equipment, tools, facilities, and institutional knowledge that can be reused from year to year.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-252) TBG became a federally recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in 2021.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-253)

The Guild’s primary mission is to reduce waste, improve efficiency, and promote continuity across successive art projects by maintaining resources that would otherwise need to be repeatedly acquired, rented, or replaced. Although it is not the recipient of Burning Man’s annual Temple grant, TBG supports Temple construction teams and other [community art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_art "Community art") projects through shared assets such as tool libraries, transportation and storage infrastructure, safety equipment, work facilities, and support services. The organization was founded on the principle that preserving tools, knowledge, and operational capacity across projects allows artists and builders to focus more on creativity and community engagement while improving the long-term sustainability of large-scale public art.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-254)

## Art

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Art")]

A hallmark of Burning Man is large-scale interactive installation art inspired by the intersection of [maker culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maker_culture "Maker culture"), technology, and nature. Many works invite participation through climbing, touch, technological interfaces, or motion. At night much of the artwork is illuminated by fire or [LEDs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light-emitting_diode "Light-emitting diode"). Creative expression through art is encouraged at Burning Man in many forms. Music, [performance art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_art "Performance art"), and [guerrilla theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_theatre "Guerrilla theatre") are art forms commonly presented within the camps and developed areas of the city. Artwork is placed in the open playa beyond the streets of the city. Each year hundreds of works of art, ranging from small to very large-scale, are brought to Black Rock City.

Art on the playa is assisted by a department of the Burning Man Project called the Artery, which helps artists place their art in the desert and ensures lighting to prevent collisions, burn platforms to protect the integrity of the dry lake bed, and that fire safety requirements are met.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-255) Art grants are available to participants via a system of curation and oversight, with application deadlines early in the year. Grants are intended to help artists produce work beyond the scope of their own means, and are generally intended to cover only a portion of the costs associated with creation of the pieces, usually requiring considerable reliance on an artist's community resources. **Burning Man** is a week-long large-scale desert event focused on "community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance" held annually in the [Western United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-2) The event's name comes from its ceremony on the second to last night of the event: the symbolic burning of a large wooden [effigy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effigy "Effigy"), referred to as the Man, the Saturday evening before [Labor Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Day "Labor Day").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-3) Since 1990, the event has been at Black Rock City in northwestern [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"), a temporary city erected in the [Black Rock Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Rock_Desert "Black Rock Desert") about 100 miles (160 km) north-northeast of [Reno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno,_Nevada "Reno, Nevada"). According to Burning Man co-founder [Larry Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Harvey "Larry Harvey") in 2004, the event is guided by ten stated principles: radical inclusion, [gifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gift_Economy "Gift Economy"), [decommodification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decommodification "Decommodification"), radical self-reliance, radical self-expression, communal effort, [civic responsibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civic_engagement "Civic engagement"), [leaving no trace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leave_no_trace "Leave no trace"), participation, and immediacy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-4)

Burning Man features no headliners or scheduled performers; participants create all the art, activities, and events.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-5) Artwork includes experimental and interactive sculptures, buildings, performances, and [art cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_car "Art car"), among other media. These contributions are inspired by a theme chosen annually by the [Burning Man Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man_Project "Burning Man Project").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-6)[NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") said of Burning Man in 2019, "Once considered an underground gathering for [bohemians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian_style "Bohemian style") and free spirits of all stripes, Burning Man has since evolved into a destination for social media influencers, celebrities and the Silicon Valley elite."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-7)

Burning Man originated on June 22, 1986, on [Baker Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Beach "Baker Beach") in San Francisco as a small function organized by Larry Harvey and Jerry James, the builders of the first Man. It has since been held annually, spanning the nine days leading up to and including [Labor Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Day "Labor Day"). Over the event's history, attendance has generally increased. In 2019, 78,850 people participated.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-8)

Burning Man is organized by the Burning Man Project, a nonprofit organization that, in 2013, succeeded Black Rock City LLC, a for-profit [limited liability company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_liability_company "Limited liability company"). Black Rock City LLC was formed in 1999 to represent the event's organizers and is now considered a subsidiary of the nonprofit organization. The Burning Man Project endorses multiple smaller regional events guided by the Burning Man principles in the United States and internationally. The 1979 film _[Stalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalker\_(1979\_film) "Stalker (1979 film)")_ by [Andrei Tarkovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Tarkovsky "Andrei Tarkovsky") heavily influenced the [Cacophony Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacophony_Society "Cacophony Society"), which began in 1986 in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") and which organized "Zone Trips" for participants.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-journal.burningman.org-9) The first burning of a wooden, symbolic man at [Black Rock Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Rock_Desert "Black Rock Desert"), Nevada, occurred on "Zone Trip Number 4" in 1990, laying the foundation for what would become the modern Burning Man.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-journal.burningman.org-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-10)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1980s")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Burning_Man_1987_poster.jpg/250px-Burning_Man_1987_poster.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burning_Man_1987_poster.jpg)

Poster for Burning Man 1987, showing the 1986 effigy

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Two-burning-man-founders.png/250px-Two-burning-man-founders.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Two-burning-man-founders.png)

Two of the founders of Burning Man: John Law (left) and Michael Mikel (right)

Burning Man began as a bonfire ritual on the summer [solstice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solstice "Solstice"). Sculptor Mary Grauberger, a friend of Larry Harvey's girlfriend, Janet Lohr, held solstice bonfire gatherings on [Baker Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Beach "Baker Beach") for several years before 1986, some of which Harvey attended. When Grauberger stopped organizing it, Harvey "picked up the torch", with Grauberger's permission, and ran with it.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Doherty_2006_28-11) He and Jerry James built the first wooden effigy on June 21, 1986, cobbled together using scrap wood, to be torched that evening. On June 22, Harvey, James, and a few friends met on [Baker Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Beach "Baker Beach") in San Francisco[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-13) and burned an 8-foot-tall (2.4 m) wooden man and a smaller wooden dog. Harvey later described his inspiration for burning these effigies as a spontaneous act of "radical self-expression".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Doherty_2006_28-11) In 1987, the Man grew to 15 feet (5 m) tall, and by 1988, it had grown to 30 feet (9 m).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-burn.life-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-:1-15)

By 1988, Harvey formally named the summer solstice ritual "Burning Man" by titling flyers for the happening as such. This was done to ward off references to "[wicker man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicker_man "Wicker man")", the reputed [Celtic pagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_paganism "Celtic paganism") practice of burning live sacrifices in human-shaped wicker cages. Harvey has said that he had not seen the 1973 [cult film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_film "Cult film")_[The Wicker Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wicker\_Man\_(1973\_film) "The Wicker Man (1973 film)")_ until many years after and that it did not inspire the action.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-burn.life-14)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-16)

### 1990 to 1996

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1990 to 1996")]

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f3/Burning_Man_1995.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original#t=151)

[8mm film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8mm_film "8mm film") footage of Burning Man in 1995 by Ammon Haggerty

Also in 1986, Kevin Evans and [John Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Law_(American_artist) "John Law (American artist)") began a series of events inspired by the Soviet film, _[Stalker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalker\_(1979\_film) "Stalker (1979 film)")_ called Zone Trips. In 1990, the fourth event of this series was planned for the remote and largely unknown [_playa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_lake "Dry lake"), also known as the [Black Rock Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Rock_Desert "Black Rock Desert"), about 110 miles (180 km) north of [Reno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno "Reno"), Nevada.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-17) Evans conceived it as a [dadaist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadaist "Dadaist")[temporary autonomous zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporary_autonomous_zone "Temporary autonomous zone") with sculptures to be burned and [situationist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Situationist_International "Situationist International") performance art. He asked John Law, who also had experience on the dry lake and was a defining founder of the [Cacophony Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacophony_Society "Cacophony Society"), to take on central organizing functions of the events. In the Cacophony Society's newsletter, it was announced as Zone Trip No. 4, A Bad Day at Black Rock (inspired by the 1955 [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Day_at_Black_Rock "Bad Day at Black Rock")).

Park police, arguing that the organizers did not have a permit, objected to the solstice burn at Baker Beach. After striking a deal to raise the Man but not to burn it, event organizers disassembled it and returned it to the vacant lot where it had been built. Shortly thereafter, the legs and torso of the Man were chain-sawed, and the pieces were removed when the space was unexpectedly leased as a parking lot. The Man was reconstructed, led by Dan Miller, Harvey's then-housemate of many years, just in time to take it to Zone Trip No. 4.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-18)

Michael Mikel, another active Cacophonist, realized that participants unfamiliar with the environment of the dry lake would benefit from knowledgeable persons helping to ensure they did not get lost in the deep dry lake and risk dehydration and death. He took the name Danger Ranger and created the Black Rock Rangers to assist them. Thus, Black Rock City began as a fellowship organized by Law and Mikel, based on Evans's and Grauberger's ideas and Harvey's and James's symbolic man. Drawing on experience in the sign business and with light sculpture, Law prepared custom neon tubes for the Man starting in 1991 so it could be seen as a beacon to aid navigation at night long before there were any planned roads.

In its early years, the community grew by word of mouth alone, and all were considered (and generally not invited until they could be expected to be) participants in their contribution to the cacophonous situationist vibe. There were no paid or scheduled performers or artists, no separation between art and life nor art space and living space, no rules other than "Don't interfere with anyone else's immediate experience" and "no guns in central camp".

1991 marked the first year that the event had a legal permit through the BLM (the [Bureau of Land Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Land_Management "Bureau of Land Management")).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-19) It was also the year that art model and fire dancer (and later Burning Man's first art director) _Crimson Rose_ attended the event.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-20) 1992 saw the birth of a smaller, intensive, nearby event named "Desert Siteworks", conceived and directed by William Binzen and co-produced (in 1993 and '94) with Judy West.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-21) There were about 20 participants the first year, and approximately 100 in the second and third year. The annual, several weeks-long event, was held over summer Solstice at various fertile hot springs surrounding the desert. Participants built art and participated in self-directed performances.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Olivier-22)

Some key organizers of Burning Man were also part of [Desert Siteworks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Siteworks "Desert Siteworks") (Law, Mikel) and Binzen was a friend of Harvey. Hence, the two events saw much cross-pollination of ideas and participants.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Olivier-22) The Desert Siteworks project ran for three years (1992–1994). 1996 was the first year a formal partnership was created to own the name "Burning Man" and was also the last year the event was held in the middle of the Black Rock Desert with no fence around it.

Before the event opened to the public in 1996, a worker named Michael Furey was killed in a motorcycle crash[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Doherty2006-23) while riding from [Gerlach, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerlach,_Nevada "Gerlach, Nevada"), to the Burning Man camp in the Black Rock Desert. Harvey insisted that the death had not occurred at Burning Man, since the gates were not yet open. Another couple were run over in their tent by an art car driving to the "rave camp", which was at that time distant from the main camp. After the 1996 event, Law [broke with Burning Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Law_(American_artist)#Founders'_conflict "John Law (American artist)") and publicly said the event should not continue.

### 1997 to 2013

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1997 to 2013")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/40/Neonman2.jpg/250px-Neonman2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Neonman2.jpg)

The neon-tubed Man at the 1999 event

1997 marked another major pivotal year for the event. It had to be moved because the permit for Black Rock was denied for the 1997 event. A team conducting land speed trials had a conflicting permit that took precedence. Fly Ranch, with the smaller adjoining Hualapai dry lakebed, just west of the Black Rock desert, was chosen as the alternate location. This moved Burning Man from Pershing County/federal BLM land into the jurisdiction of [Washoe County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washoe_County,_Nevada "Washoe County, Nevada"), which brought a protracted list of permit requirements.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-24)

In 1999 to comply with the new requirements and manage the increased liability load, Harvey and five organizers formed Black Rock City LLC with the assistance of "Biz Babe" [Dana Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Harrison "Dana Harrison"). The LLC founders consisted of Larry Harvey (chief philosophy officer), Harley K. DuBois (chief transition officer), Marian Goodell (CEO), Crimson Rose (art transition officer), Will Roger Peterson (Nevada relations director), and Michael Mikel (historian and archivist).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-25)

Will Roger Peterson and Flynn Mauthe created the Black Rock City Department of Public Works (DPW) to build the "city" grid layout (a requirement so that emergency vehicles could be directed to an "address"), designed by Rod Garrett, an architect. Garrett continued as the city designer until his death in 2011, at age 76. He is also credited with the design of all of the Man bases from 2001 through 2012, the center camp café and first camp.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-26) 1998 saw a return to the Black Rock desert, although not to the deep playa, along with a temporary perimeter fence. The event has remained there since.

As the population of Black Rock City grew, the BLM added more restrictions, and changes were made in how people were invited to the event, notably the addition of publicized online ticket sales to all comers; further rules were established concerning its survival. Some critics of the later phase of the event cite these rules as impinging on the original freedoms and principles, diminishing the scope of the experience unacceptably, while many newer attendees find the increased level of activity more than balances out the changes:

*   A grid street structure.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-27)
*   A speed limit of 5 mph (8 km/h).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-dmv-28)
*   A ban on driving, except for approved "mutant vehicles" and service vehicles.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-29)
*   Safety standards on mutant vehicles.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-dmv-28)
*   Burning of any art must be done on an approved burn platform.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-burningman.com-30)
*   A ban on fireworks.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-31)
*   A ban on animals.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-32)

Another notable restriction to attendees is the 9.2-mile- (14.8 km) long[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-33) temporary plastic fence that surrounds the event and defines the pentagon of land used by the event on the southern edge of the Black Rock dry lake.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-34) This 4-foot- (1.2-meter) high barrier is known as the "trash fence" because its initial use was to catch wind-blown debris that might escape from campsites during the event. Since 2002, the area beyond this fence has not been accessible to Burning Man participants during the event.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-35)

One visitor who was accidentally burned at the 2005 event unsuccessfully sued Black Rock City LLC in [San Francisco County Superior Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_County_Superior_Court "San Francisco County Superior Court"). On June 30, 2009, the [California Court of Appeal for the First District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_courts_of_appeal "California courts of appeal") upheld the trial court's grant of [summary judgment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summary_judgment "Summary judgment") to Black Rock City LLC on the basis that people who deliberately walk toward The Man after it is ignited [assume the risk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_of_risk "Assumption of risk") of getting burned by such a hazardous object.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-36)

### 2013 to 2019

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2013 to 2019")]

In December 2013, following negotiations between founders,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-37) Black Rock City LLC was made a subsidiary of a new nonprofit entity known as the [Burning Man Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man_Project "Burning Man Project").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-40)

On September 3, 2017,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-41) a 41-year-old man, Aaron Joel Mitchell, fought his way past a safety cordon of volunteers and firefighters and threw himself into the flames of the Man. Mitchell died the next day due to cardiac arrest, bodily shock, and third-degree burns to 97% of his body. His death was ruled a suicide.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-44)

### 2020 to 2021

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 to 2021")]

On April 10, 2020, the Burning Man Project announced that Burning Man was canceled for 2020[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-45) due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), making 2020 the first year Burning Man did not happen since its inception. They then decided to offer ticket refunds despite the tickets being sold explicitly as non-refundable.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-46)

On September 7, 2020, an estimated 1,000 Burners celebrated on San Francisco's [Ocean Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Beach,_San_Francisco "Ocean Beach, San Francisco"). San Francisco Mayor [London Breed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Breed "London Breed") tweeted about the event, "This was reckless and selfish. You aren't celebrating, but are putting people's lives and our progress at risk. No one is immune from spreading the virus."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-47) Several thousand also showed up in the Black Rock desert for an unofficial event and some described it as a return to the "old days".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Forbes2020-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-RGJ2020a-49)

The 2021 event was canceled on April 27, 2021, due to the continuation of the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite progress on vaccination, organizers said that "uncertainties that need to be resolved are impossible to resolve in the time we have".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-50) On May 14, 2021, the Burning Man Project released tickets on their website for online events slated between August 22 and September 7, 2021.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-51)

The unofficial event was more extensive than in 2020, with an estimated 20,000 attending. Various groups loosely coordinated it, including Black Rock Plan B and Rogue Burn. The [Bureau of Land Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Land_Management "Bureau of Land Management") implemented restrictions including no structures other than shade structures and no fires other than campfires. There was a massive illuminated [drone display](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_display "Drone display") outlining the Man instead of the burning of a Man effigy.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-RGJ2021a-52)

### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

Main article: [Burning Man 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man_2023 "Burning Man 2023")

The 2023 Burning Man had rains and subsequent flooding on Labor Day weekend, with a lockdown preventing vehicle movement throughout the site.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-54) Organizers arranged for some cellular service and shared a 2023 Wet Playa Survival Guide: "no driving is permitted until the playa surface dries up, with the exception of emergency services… Participants are encouraged to conserve food, water, and fuel, and shelter in a warm, safe space" and told attendees about Burning Man Information Radio (BMIR) 94.5 FM and Gate Information Radio Station (GARS) 95.1.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-55) One person died following the flooding, with thousands more stranded.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-56)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2024")]

On August 25, 2024, the first day of the 2024 Burning Man event, a female participant died.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-58) On August 26, it was reported that tickets remained unsold for the event for the first time since 2011.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-notsoldout-59) As ticket sales lagged, the organizers asked large-scale sound camps' DJs to drive ticket sales by announcing their lineups early. This conflicted with the event's principle of [decommodification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decommodification "Decommodification"). Some camps declined the request or responded satirically; the art car Robot Heart released its lineup as a game of hangman.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-60)

An epic dust storm was reported on the final day of the event, snarling departure traffic and causing lines to last more than four hours.

The Burning Man Project engaged in a fundraising campaign that began in October 2024. The campaign aims to collect $20 million. In December 2024, CEO Marian Goodell emailed supporters that the project still requires $14 million to meet its financial goal for the 2025 event.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-61)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2025")]

The 2025 Burning Man event opened on August 24, 2025, and ran until September 1, 2025.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-62) However, shortly before the opening, it was reported that the event once again failed to have a sell-out attendance and that ongoing financial problems persisted.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-financialstate2025-63)_[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business\_Insider "Business Insider")_ stated that the annual event was now in a "precarious financial situation."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-financialstate2025-63) At the time the event began, massive dust storms occurred.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-2025festivalanalysis-66) On August 27, 2025, it was revealed that the event's "Orgy Dome," which had been in use at the event since 2003, had collapsed due to strong desert winds.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-68) It was afterwards announced that it would not be restored for the year.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-69) Gates also closed intermittently because of heavy rain, with one participant being electrocuted.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-70) On August 30, a man was found dead at the event.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-71)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-2025festivalanalysis-66) The victim was later identified as 37-year-old Vadim Kruglov, a [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") resident originally from Russia. Police are treating it as a homicide.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-72)

### 2026

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2026")]

The 2026 Burning Man festival ran from August 30 through September 7.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-sg2026-73) Three attendees died during the event; two on the festival grounds, and one in transit to a local hospital.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-guard-8sep2026-74)

## Event timeline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Event timeline")]

The statistics below illustrate the growth in both the scale and scope of Burning Man in terms of location, height of the central Man sculpture, population, ticket price, and several registered camps and art.

After starting at 8 ft (2.4 m) and growing taller each of the next three years, the height of the titular Man remained at 40 ft (12 m) between 1989 and 2013. During those years, changes in the size and form of the base on which the wooden Man stood accounted for the differing heights of the overall structures.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-timeline-75) In 2014 the construction of the Man changed to a 105 ft (32 m) tall figure standing directly on the ground with no base. From 2015 to 2019 the Man returned to 40 ft (12 m) in height.

### Population counts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Population counts")]

The population count is a stipulation of the Special Recreation Permit (SRP) granted to the Burning Man Project, formerly Black Rock City, LLC (BRC), by the BLM, for the event each year. Originally used to calculate fees, it's now used to ensure that the event does not exceed the maximum authorized population as specified in the SRP. Not everyone at the event is included in the population count. Exempted from the count are government personnel and government contractors; however, this has changed over time.

The population count was originally used to calculate fees owed to the BLM. It was not long until the BLM began considering putting a limit on the number of people that would be allowed to attend the event. This became a point of contention as early as 1998 when the BLM proposed a complicated usage formula, effectively limiting the size of the event to that of the previous year.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Larry-196)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-197)

Starting in 2006, the SRP stipulated that BRC manage "ticket sales in a manner to keep the maximum population of the event from increasing more than 6% above the highest population recorded in a previous year."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):1 Fees were based on the daily population counts of Black Rock City at noon.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):12 This was the first year where fees were explicitly exempted for BRC staff.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2006-108):12.

In 2011, the fee structure changed to be based on adjusted gross income and was no longer tied to daily population counts.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-198):5

The 2012 SRP further defined who was to be counted in population counts. The term "participant" was introduced, as defined in that year's Environmental Assessment (EA), to include "all attendees of the event, including paid participants and volunteers. The population does not include government personnel, Humboldt General Hospital emergency service providers, vendors and contractors."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-199):2–1 The maximum authorized population now applied to "participants".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2012-129):1

In 2014, volunteers were explicitly exempted from the population count and the population cap was further refined to now apply to "paid participants".[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2014-139):1

In 2019, the definition of "population" changed again, this time to include BRC staff and volunteers, now collectively referred to as "attendees".[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2019-165):1 This coincided with the necessity of a new Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the 2019–2028 SRP application which introduced this change in definition.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-200):ES-1 The Burning Man Project reported a population of 78,850 for that year, an increase of about 8,600 people from the previous year, noting that "everyone" was now being counted in the maximum population count.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Timeline-201) This roughly correlates with the Burning Man Project's 2019 Form 990 disclosure which states it employs 986 people and has 10,000 volunteers.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-202):1

In 2022, an additional restriction on the total number of attendees for the entirety of the event was introduced. "The cumulative maximum authorized population for the 2022 event is 87,000 total attendees." The maximum number of attendees on the playa at any one time remained as it was in 2019 at 80,000.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-SRP_2022-179):1

## Principles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Principles")]

The man effigy with fireworks before being burned in 2011

Because of the variety of goals fostered by participatory attendees, known as "Burners," Burning Man does not have a single focus. Features of the event are subject to the participants and include _community_, _artwork_, _absurdity_, _decommodification_ and _revelry_. Participation is encouraged.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-203)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-204)

The Burning Man event and its affiliated communities are guided by 10 principles meant to evoke the cultural ethos that has emerged from the event. They were originally written by Larry Harvey in 2004[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-205) as guidelines for regional organizing, then later became universal criteria of the general culture of the multifaceted movement. The 10 Principles are:[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-principles-206)

*   radical [inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion_(value_and_practice) "Inclusion (value and practice)")
*   gifting
*   [decommodification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decommodification "Decommodification")
*   radical [self-reliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-sufficiency "Self-sufficiency")
*   radical [self-expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_expression "Emotional expression")
*   [communal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community "Community") effort
*   civic [responsibility](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/responsibility "wikt:responsibility")
*   [leaving no trace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leave_No_Trace "Leave No Trace")
*   participation
*   immediacy

The descriptions in quotes are the actual text:

### Radical inclusion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Radical inclusion")]

"Anyone may be a part of Burning Man. We welcome and respect the stranger. No prerequisites exist for participation in our community." This was written with a broad stroke for general organizing, meaning anyone is welcome to the Burning Man culture. Prerequisites for the Burning Man[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-principles-206) event are: participants are expected to provide for their own basic needs, follow the guidelines in the annually updated event "survival guide", and purchase a $475 ticket to get in.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-survivalguide-207)

### Gifting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Gifting")]

"Burning Man is devoted to acts of gift-giving. The value of a gift is unconditional. Gifting does not contemplate a return or an exchange for something of equal value." Instead of cash, burners are encouraged to rely on a [gift economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gift_economy "Gift economy"), a sort of [potlatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potlatch "Potlatch"). In the earliest days of the event, an underground [barter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barter "Barter") economy also existed, in which burners exchanged "favors" with each other. While this was originally supported by the Burning Man organization, it is now largely discouraged. Instead, burners are encouraged to give one another gifts unconditionally. Despite the efforts of the Burning Man organization, bartering still continues to be very common across certain camps.

### Decommodification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Decommodification")]

"To preserve the spirit of gifting, our community seeks to create social environments that are unmediated by commercial sponsorships, transactions, or advertising. We stand ready to protect our culture from such exploitation. We resist the substitution of consumption for participatory experience." No cash transactions are permitted between burners. Cash can be used for a select few charity, fuel, and sanitation vendors as follows:[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-208)

*   Café beverages such as coffee, [chai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_chai "Masala chai"), [lemonade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemonade "Lemonade"), etc., which are sold at Center Camp Café, operated by the organizers of the event.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-209) Citing cost, decreased need, environmental impact, and decommodification, beverage sales were halted in 2022.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-210)
*   [Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice "Ice") sales benefit the local [Gerlach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerlach,_Nevada "Gerlach, Nevada")-[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire,_Nevada "Empire, Nevada") school system.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-211)
*   Tickets for the shuttle bus to the nearest Nevada communities of Gerlach and Empire which is operated by a contractor not participating in the event: [Green Tortoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Tortoise "Green Tortoise").[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-212)
*   A reentry wristband, which allows a person to leave and reenter the event and may be purchased at the gate upon exit.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-213)
*   An airport use fee, payable at the airport upon first entry.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-214)
*   Diesel and biodiesel sold by third-party contractors.
*   RV dump service and camp [graywater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graywater "Graywater") disposal service.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-215)
*   Private portable toilets and servicing, which can be arranged with the official contractor.

### Radical self-reliance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Radical self-reliance")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Burning_Man_2012_%287942014474%29.jpg/250px-Burning_Man_2012_%287942014474%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burning_Man_2012_(7942014474).jpg)

Dust storms are common at Burning Man, so many come prepared with appropriate protection such as goggles and masks to reduce dust inhalation.

"Burning Man encourages the individual to discover, exercise, and rely on his or her inner resources." The event's harsh environment and remote location require participants to be responsible for their subsistence. Since the LLC forbids most commerce, participants must be prepared and bring all their own supplies with the exception of the items stated in Decommodification.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-216) Public portable toilets are also available throughout the city; some of these are, like art cars, decorated in imaginative ways by volunteers.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-217)

### Radical self-expression

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Radical self-expression")]

[Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b7/Trojan_Horse_Pull_-_Burning_Man_2011.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Trojan Horse Pull – Burning Man 2011

"Radical self-expression arises from the unique gifts of the individual. No one other than the individual or a collaborating group can determine its content. It is offered as a gift to others. In this spirit, the giver should respect the rights and liberties of the recipient." Burners are encouraged to express themselves in a number of ways through various art forms and projects. The event is clothing-optional and [public nudity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_nudity "Public nudity") is common, though not practiced by the majority.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-OpenSex-218)[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-Illicit_Activities-219)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-220)

### Communal effort

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Communal effort")]

"Our community values creative cooperation and collaboration. We strive to produce, promote and protect social networks, public spaces, works of art, and methods of communication that support such interaction." Burners are encouraged to work with and help one another.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man#cite_note-participate-221)

### Civic responsibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Civic responsibility")]

"We value civil society. Community members who organize events should assume responsibility for public welfare and endeavor to communicate civic responsibilities to participants. They must also assume responsibility for conducting events in accordance with local, state and federal laws."

### Leave no trace

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Leave no trace")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg/250px-Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shinobi_walks_the_line.jpg)

Burning Man Playa Restoration 2015 – attendees carry sticks and buckets to clean the desert of MOOP (matter out of place), as part of the "leave no trace" policy.

"Our community respects the environment. We are committed to leaving no physical trace of our activities wherever we gather. We clean up after ourselves and endeavor, whenever possible, to leave such places in a better state than when we found them."

### Participation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Participation")]

"Our community is committed to a radically participatory ethic. We believe that transformative change, whether in the individual or in society, can occur only through the medium of deeply personal participation. We achieve being through doing. Everyone is invited to work. Everyone is invited to play. We make the world real through actions that open the heart." People are encouraged to participate, rather than observe.

### Immediacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Burning_Man&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Immediacy")]

"Immediate experience is, in many ways, the most important touchstone of value in our culture. We seek to overcome barriers that stand between us and a recognition of our inner selves, the reality of those around us, participation in society, and contact with a natural world exceeding human powers. No idea can substitute for this experience."

The Temple is the secondary major recurring art installation at Burning Man after the Man, and is considered just as important to the event culture. ## About This Data

### What Is This Data?

Nonprofit Explorer includes summary data for nonprofit tax returns and full Form 990 documents, in both PDF and digital formats.

The summary data contains information processed by the IRS during the 2012-2019 calendar years; this generally consists of filings for the 2011-2018 fiscal years, but may include older records. This data release includes only a subset of what can be found in the full Form 990s.

In addition to the raw summary data, we link to PDFs and digital copies of full Form 990 documents wherever possible. This consists of separate releases by the IRS of Form 990 documents processed by the agency, which we update regularly.

We also link to copies of audits nonprofit organizations that spent $750,000 or more in Federal grant money in a single fiscal year since 2016. These audits are copied from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.

### Which Organizations Are Here?

Every organization that has been recognized as tax exempt by the IRS has to file Form 990 every year, unless they make less than $200,000 in revenue and have less than $500,000 in assets, in which case they have to file form 990-EZ. Organizations making less than $50,000 don’t have to file either form but do have to let the IRS they’re still in business via a [Form 990N "e-Postcard."](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/annual-electronic-filing-requirement-for-small-exempt-organizations-form-990-n-e-postcard)

Nonprofit Explorer has organizations claiming tax exemption in each of the 27 subsections of the 501(c) section of the tax code, and which have filed a Form 990, Form 990EZ or Form 990PF. Taxable trusts and private foundations that are required to file a form 990PF are also included. Small organizations filing a Form 990N "e-Postcard" are not included in this data.

### Types of Nonprofits

There are 27 nonprofit designations based on the numbered subsections of section 501(c) of the tax code. [See the list »](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/ctypes)

### Get the Data

For those interested in acquiring the original data from the source, here’s where our data comes from:

*   [Raw filing data](https://www.irs.gov/uac/soi-tax-stats-annual-extract-of-tax-exempt-organization-financial-data). Includes EINs and summary financials as structured data. 
*   [Exempt Organization profiles](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf). Includes organization names, addresses, etc. You can merge this with the raw filing data using EIN numbers. 
*   [Form 990 documents](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). Prior to 2017, these documents were obtained and processed by [Public.Resource.org](https://public.resource.org/) and ProPublica. Bulk PDF downloads since 2017 are available from [the IRS](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). 
*   [Form 990 documents as XML files](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). Includes complete filing data (financial details, names of officers, tax schedules, etc.) in machine-readable format. Only available for electronically filed documents. Electronic data released prior to October 2021 is also available [through Amazon Web Services.](https://registry.opendata.aws/irs990/)
*   [Audits](https://harvester.census.gov/facdissem/Main.aspx). PDFs of single or program-specific audits for nonprofit organizations that spent $750,000 or more in Federal grant money in a single fiscal year. Available for fiscal year 2015 and later.

## About This Data

### What Is This Data?

Nonprofit Explorer includes summary data for nonprofit tax returns and full Form 990 documents, in both PDF and digital formats.

The summary data contains information processed by the IRS during the 2012-2019 calendar years; this generally consists of filings for the 2011-2018 fiscal years, but may include older records. This data release includes only a subset of what can be found in the full Form 990s.

In addition to the raw summary data, we link to PDFs and digital copies of full Form 990 documents wherever possible. This consists of separate releases by the IRS of Form 990 documents processed by the agency, which we update regularly.

We also link to copies of audits nonprofit organizations that spent $750,000 or more in Federal grant money in a single fiscal year since 2016. These audits are copied from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.

### Which Organizations Are Here?

Every organization that has been recognized as tax exempt by the IRS has to file Form 990 every year, unless they make less than $200,000 in revenue and have less than $500,000 in assets, in which case they have to file form 990-EZ. Organizations making less than $50,000 don’t have to file either form but do have to let the IRS they’re still in business via a [Form 990N "e-Postcard."](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/annual-electronic-filing-requirement-for-small-exempt-organizations-form-990-n-e-postcard)

Nonprofit Explorer has organizations claiming tax exemption in each of the 27 subsections of the 501(c) section of the tax code, and which have filed a Form 990, Form 990EZ or Form 990PF. Taxable trusts and private foundations that are required to file a form 990PF are also included. Small organizations filing a Form 990N "e-Postcard" are not included in this data.

### Types of Nonprofits

There are 27 nonprofit designations based on the numbered subsections of section 501(c) of the tax code. [See the list »](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/ctypes)

### Get the Data

For those interested in acquiring the original data from the source, here’s where our data comes from:

*   [Raw filing data](https://www.irs.gov/uac/soi-tax-stats-annual-extract-of-tax-exempt-organization-financial-data). Includes EINs and summary financials as structured data. 
*   [Exempt Organization profiles](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf). Includes organization names, addresses, etc. You can merge this with the raw filing data using EIN numbers. 
*   [Form 990 documents](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). Prior to 2017, these documents were obtained and processed by [Public.Resource.org](https://public.resource.org/) and ProPublica. Bulk PDF downloads since 2017 are available from [the IRS](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). 
*   [Form 990 documents as XML files](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads). Includes complete filing data (financial details, names of officers, tax schedules, etc.) in machine-readable format. Only available for electronically filed documents. Electronic data released prior to October 2021 is also available [through Amazon Web Services.](https://registry.opendata.aws/irs990/)
*   [Audits](https://harvester.census.gov/facdissem/Main.aspx). PDFs of single or program-specific audits for nonprofit organizations that spent $750,000 or more in Federal grant money in a single fiscal year. Available for fiscal year 2015 and later.
